fields.Front: What kind of data store is Redis, and what roles is it commonly used for?
fields.Back: An in-memory key-value data store, optionally persisted to disk — commonly used as a cache, message broker, or fast primary store for counters/sessions.

fields.Front: Write a Redis command to set a key with a 60-second expiry.
What does TTL stand for in Redis, and what does the TTL command return?
fields.Back: Time To Live — returns the remaining seconds until a key expires (-1 if it has no expiry, -2 if the key doesn't exist).
On read, check the cache first; on a miss, fetch from the source of truth (e.g. the DB), then write the result into the cache before returning it.

fields.Front: In cache-aside, what must the application do on a write to keep the cache from serving stale data?
fields.Back: Invalidate (or update) the corresponding cache entry right after writing to the source of truth.

fields.Front: What Redis command publishes a message to a channel in pub/sub?
What's the key limitation of Redis pub/sub compared to a durable message queue?
fields.Back: Messages aren't persisted — a subscriber that isn't connected at publish time never receives that message.

fields.Front: Why is INCR atomic in Redis, and why does that matter for counters?
fields.Back: Redis executes each command as one indivisible step, so INCR reads and writes the counter atomically — avoiding lost updates from concurrent clients incrementing the same key.

fields.Front: Write a Redis command to atomically increment a page-view counter.
Which Redis data type is best suited for a leaderboard ranked by score, and why?
fields.Back: Sorted set (ZSET) — each member has a score, and Redis keeps members ordered for fast range and rank queries.

fields.Front: Write a Redis command to add a player's score to a leaderboard sorted set.
When would you choose Redis as the primary data store rather than only a cache?
fields.Back: When the workload needs very low-latency reads/writes on data that fits in memory and can tolerate Redis's persistence/durability tradeoffs — e.g. session stores, rate limiters, real-time counters.

fields.Front: What Redis command retrieves and removes the first element of a list, useful for a queue?
What's the difference between EXPIRE and PERSIST in Redis?
fields.Back: EXPIRE sets a TTL so the key auto-deletes after that time; PERSIST removes any existing TTL, making the key permanent again.
